items.followUp: What type of intermolecular forces act between water molecules?

rubric.why: Identifies the characteristic attraction between polar HCl molecules.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying dipole–dipole attraction.

rubric.why: Shows why HCl molecules attract through this force.
rubric.description: Recognizes that HCl molecules are polar.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that HCl is polar.

modelAnswer: Dipole–dipole forces exist between HCl molecules.

items.followUp: State one difference between boiling and condensation.

rubric.why: Identifies evaporation as the change from liquid to gas.
rubric.description: States the direction of change in evaporation.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for liquid changing into vapour or gas.

rubric.why: Identifies condensation as the change from gas to liquid.
rubric.description: States the direction of change in condensation.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for vapour or gas changing into liquid.

modelAnswer: Evaporation is the change of a liquid into vapour from its surface.
Condensation is the change of vapour into liquid.

items.followUp: Define isotopes and give one example.

rubric.why: Captures the defining idea of allotropy.
rubric.description: Defines allotropy as an element occurring in different forms in the same physical state.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that the same element exists in different forms in the same physical state.

rubric.why: Provides a valid example of allotropy.
rubric.description: Gives an example, such as diamond and graphite.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a valid allotrope example.

modelAnswer: Allotropy is the property of an element to exist in two or more different forms in the same physical state.
For example, carbon exists as diamond and graphite.

items.followUp: What is meant by a saturated solution?

rubric.why: Identifies water as the solvent in an aqueous solution.
rubric.description: States that water is the solvent.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying water as the solvent.

rubric.why: Explains that a solution contains dissolved substance.
rubric.description: States that a solute or substance is dissolved in the water.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that a substance is dissolved in water.

modelAnswer: An aqueous solution is a solution in which water is the solvent.
A solute is dissolved in the water.

items.followUp: Define a colloidal solution and give one example.

rubric.why: Describes the dispersed solid particles in a suspension.
rubric.description: States that a suspension is a heterogeneous mixture of insoluble solid particles in a liquid.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the defining composition or heterogeneous nature of a suspension.

rubric.description: Gives a valid example of a suspension.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for an appropriate example.

modelAnswer: A suspension is a heterogeneous mixture in which insoluble solid particles are dispersed in a liquid and can settle on standing.
Muddy water is an example of a suspension.

items.followUp: Give two examples of liquid-in-liquid solutions.

rubric.why: Brass is a solid solution (alloy) of copper and zinc.
rubric.description: Gives brass or its constituent metals as one example.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for brass or copper and zinc.

rubric.why: Bronze is a solid solution (alloy) of copper and tin.
rubric.description: Gives bronze or its constituent metals as another example.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for bronze or copper and tin.

modelAnswer: Brass (copper and zinc) is a solid-in-solid solution.
Bronze (copper and tin) is another solid-in-solid solution.

items.followUp: Define a weak electrolyte and give one example.

rubric.why: States the defining degree of ionization or dissociation.
rubric.description: Says that a strong electrolyte completely ionizes or dissociates in solution.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for complete ionization or dissociation.

rubric.why: Provides a valid strong electrolyte example.
rubric.description: Gives an example such as sodium chloride, hydrochloric acid, or sodium hydroxide.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a correct example.

modelAnswer: A strong electrolyte completely ionizes or dissociates into ions in aqueous solution.

items.followUp: Write two uses of potassium metal.

rubric.why: Recognizes a common use of sodium in lighting.
rubric.description: States that sodium is used in sodium-vapour lamps or street lighting.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a correct lighting use.

rubric.why: Recognizes another accepted use of sodium metal.
rubric.description: States a use such as coolant in nuclear reactors or as a reducing agent.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for another valid use.

modelAnswer: Sodium is used in sodium-vapour lamps for street lighting.
It is used as a coolant in nuclear reactors.
